next_question: Does iterative decompression (decompress repeatedly until failure or a maximum depth of 3-5) restore decompressed body-only discrimination to >= 0.3 and decompressed hash determinism (all_same=true) under double-brotli and triple-brotli encoding on localhost — and does it maintain discrimination for the 4 single-layer encoding scenarios that already pass?
why_next: Double-brotli encoding with single-pass client decompression is the sole failure mode: discrimination 0.2911 < 0.3 and determinism fails (2 unique hashes per state). Audit V6 confirms iterative decompression (brotli decompress twice) recovers the true body. The 4 single-layer scenarios (correct_br, missing_ce, incorrect_gzip, garbled_ce) all produce identical decompressed hashes, so the mechanism is not fundamentally broken — the client implementation is insufficient. Testing iterative decompression is the smallest change that could restore the claim ceiling. Real CDN infrastructure should be deferred until iterative-decompression is validated locally, because testing CDN with a known-broken client would confound CDN effects with client implementation effects.

established: Decompression-normalization (SHA256 on decompressed body + status) survives single-layer encoding non-determinism: correct_br, missing Content-Encoding, incorrect gzip label, and garbled Content-Encoding all produce identical decompressed hashes for the same auth state and content type. 4/5 encoding scenarios pass determinism (all_same=true within scenario). Verified across all 9 content-type x size combinations (JSON/HTML/XML x 1KB/10KB/100KB).
Discrimination without double_br is 0.4486 (above 0.3 threshold), confirming the mechanism works when decompression fully succeeds.

B-RANDOM null control passes at 0.0 for all 9 conditions. C_ENCODING_VARIATION_EXISTS passes (5/5 scenarios observed per condition). C_GRACEFUL_DEGRADATION passes (0 crashes/hangs from garbled headers).

Parent EXP-RUNTIME-35237982464 established: discrimination 0.5 under non-deterministic brotli quality variation {4,5,6,7,8} on localhost, algorithm equivalence (brotli vs gzip), determinism under quality variation (all_same=true), compressed-only discrimination lower than decompressed (0.16-0.35 vs 0.50), structural ceiling 0.5 from 3-way error collapse.
rejected: Single-pass client decompression does NOT survive double-brotli encoding: discrimination 0.2911 < 0.3, decompressed hash variation all_same=false with 2 unique per state. The double_br scenario produces a hash of the still-inner-compressed data (ddd198...) rather than the true decompressed body (6fb10...).

B-IDENTITY-FALLBACK baseline was NOT exercised: missing_ce and garbled_ce scenarios still succeed via brotli fallback (decompression_errors=[]), so the identity-fallback discrimination path was never tested.

B-COMPRESSED-BYTE-ONLY baseline is INCONCLUSIVE: compressed and decompressed discrimination are identical (0.2911) in this encoding-proxy setting because double_br decompressed equals compressed intermediate.

do_not_assume: Do NOT assume decompression-normalization is production-ready — real CDN infrastructure is untested and is the critical remaining blocker after iterative-decompression fix.
Do NOT assume the structural discrimination ceiling of 0.5 applies to production environments — it is a property of the 3-way error collapse mock design.

Do NOT assume single-pass decompression is adequate for production — double-brotli encoding is a realistic CDN scenario (CDN edge compresses already-compressed origin responses, or intermediate proxies add compression).
Do NOT assume the localhost decompression latency (0.01-0.28ms) represents production cost.
Do NOT assume format-invariance extends to binary content types or compressed data formats.
Do NOT assume non-deterministic quality is equivalent to real CDN behavior — real CDNs also vary caching, chunked encoding, Accept-Encoding negotiation, and edge selection.
